Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and agreed next steps so we have alignment heading into the PoC ramp: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 150ms for short text generation (<= 128 tokens)
- Throughput target: sustained ~400 tokens/sec aggregate across the service during peak windows
- Concurrency: ~120 parallel requests from your app (connection pooling from 12 app hosts averaging 10 concurrent requests each)
- Streaming: yes — low-latency chunked streaming to client with partial tokens as they arrive
- Failover: automatic fallback to smaller model variant for tail-load scenarios

Open items we promised to follow up on:
1) Concrete rate-limit / quota proposal for the above concurrency pattern
2) A simple connection pooling guidance doc and recommended SDK settings (keep-alive, maxConnectionsPerHost)
3) Technical diagram of routing + KV cache behavior under high concurrency (attached)
4) Estimated monthly committed capacity and initial Dedicated pool sizing for PoC

Next steps:
- I attached a short proposal outlining the rate-limit tiers we recommend for your expected traffic, plus a concurrency diagram (redwood-rate-limit-proposal.pdf, concurrency-diagram.png).
- Vivek will send a short note on preferred connection pooling settings and how to tune the SDK for streaming.
- Aditya will follow up with commercial terms and a draft SOW for the PoC.

Can you confirm the concurrency numbers above are correct (120 parallel requests, 12 hosts)? If either number is off, tell us and we’ll re-run the capacity calc.

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Confirming the concurrency numbers: those are correct — we expect ~12 app hosts with peak of 10 concurrent streaming requests per host, so ~120 parallel connections.

A couple of clarifications: 
- The 400 tokens/sec is an aggregate target across all clients, but some single-user flows may burst to 50 tokens/sec for ~10s windows. We care more about 95th/99th P99 latency for user-facing calls than absolute p50.
- For failover, small-model fallback is acceptable if we can guarantee throughput and that quality drop is limited for the short queries.

Hi all —

Quick technical answers to Sana's questions: 
- Redwood enforces rate limits at the API key level by default (per-customer token). We also support per-IP shaping for private deployments if you want network-level guards.
- Default burst window: we support a short burst (token-bucket) of roughly 3x your sustained rate for ~30s before smoothing kicks in; we can adjust burst/bucket settings for committed customers.
- For your connection pooling pattern (12 hosts x 10 conns), we recommend SDK settings: maxConnectionsPerHost=16, connectionKeepAlive=60s, idleTimeout=90s. Those settings keep head-of-line blocking low while allowing Redwood's routing to batch efficiently.
- For streaming, use HTTP/2 or our websocket gateway (we recommend HTTP/2). Use a long-lived connection per host with multiple concurrent streams rather than opening/closing connections per request.

I've attached a small diagram showing where token-bucket shaping applies and how fallback routes get selected when concurrency exceeds the Dedicated pool (see concurrency-diagram.png).

If you want, we can propose two quota tiers for the PoC: 
A) PoC tier (shared burstable): 120 concurrent requests limit, soft quota of 10M tokens/month, default burst 3x for 30s.
B) Committed Dedicated tier: reserved 200 concurrency, hard quota based on committed throughput, custom burst settings and higher SLA.

I'll hand this back to Marissa/Aditya for commercialization.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
